_doc: Island-bound passenger capacity per hour, used to turn forecast boardings into busyness levels (share of practical capacity). See README 'Busyness levels' and reports/model_report.md. Sources: City of Toronto fleet page (Ongiara 216, William Inglis 395, Sam McBride 908, Thomas Rennie 908 passengers; new electric ferries 1,300 from 2027) and the City ferry schedule page (winter Oct 14 - mid-April: Ward's Island only, ~25 departures/day; spring/fall: reduced trips on all routes; summer mid-May - mid-September: all routes, Centre Island every 15-40 min). Nominal = vessels x departures per hour; practical = nominal x load_factor (boats are never 100% full in practice). The busiest hour ever recorded (3,737 boardings, 2026-07-11 13:00) is ~77% of the peak-summer nominal capacity.
_level_shares_doc: Share of PRACTICAL capacity at which each level starts. Most riders take the Centre Island boats, which fill first: at 65% of practical capacity in peak summer (~2,500 boardings/h) the Centre boats are near-full and people start waiting for the next one, matching reports of 30-60 min waits on summer weekends. Busy (40%, ~1,550/h in peak summer) = lines at the gates, boats filling. Moderate (20%) = steady but walk-on.

winter.basis: Ward's Island only: William Inglis (395) or Ongiara (216), up to ~2 departures/h midday

spring.basis: reduced trips, all routes: one 908-seat boat ~1.3/h to Centre, Inglis ~1/h, Ongiara ~1.5/h

summer.basis: all routes, Centre Island every 30-40 min with two 908-seat boats, Hanlan's/Ward's every 30-60 min

summer_peak.basis: school summer break to Labour Day: Centre every 15-30 min (2 x 908 seats x 2/h), Inglis 2/h to Hanlan's, Ongiara 2/h to Ward's

overrides.basis: Sam McBride (908) out of service after the 2022-08-20 dock crash; modified schedule for the rest of the summer (Global News, 2022-08-21)
